label: Sodium nitroprusside
summary: Fast-acting, short half-life vasodilator of arteries and veins. It lowers afterload and preload and is titrated minute to minute, usually with an arterial line.

levers.why: Arterial dilation lowers the pressure the LV ejects against.
Venous dilation lowers return to the heart.

nursingPriorities: Use continuous arterial BP monitoring and titrate exactly per order.
Protect from light per the label, and watch for cyanide or thiocyanate toxicity with high doses, long infusions, or kidney or liver dysfunction.

relations.why: Vasodilation can drop BP sharply when output is fixed by a narrowed valve.
Hypotension worsens coronary and organ perfusion, so it is used only when MAP allows.
